The user wants to improve or evaluate the MythosMini model, which is a byte-level transformer trained on fineweb-edu. They have a fairly complex pipeline and are likely interested in advanced distillation techniques that can handle mismatched tokenizers, especially converting teacher logits (which are likely wordpiece or BPE) to supervision for a byte-level student. 

From the earlier searches, I found several recent papers on cross-tokenizer distillation. The most relevant seems to be “Cross-Tokenizer LLM Distillation through a Byte-Level Interface” (arXiv ID 2604.07466v1). This paper directly addresses the problem of converting teacher token-level logits into byte-level supervision, which matches exactly the scenario we have: a byte-level student (MythosMini) and a typical subword teacher. The user explicitly asked for a summary of that paper, focusing on the exact method, conversion process, experimental setup (teachers/students, compute), and results compared to baselines like ULD, MinED, and synthetic-data SeqKD, plus any released code.

Thus, the next logical step is to retrieve the full paper content so I can extract those details. The best tool for this is WebFetch, which can pull the HTML (or PDF) from the arXiv URL. I will request the URL https://arxiv.org/html/2604.07466v1 and include a prompt that asks the tool to summarize the paper with the specific questions the user has. This will give me a concise answer that directly addresses their needs without me having to manually parse the PDF.

Therefore, I will invoke the WebFetch tool with the appropriate URL and prompt.
